final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse, supported by a 45-billion CHF hard cap on legacy losses (shared between SNB and UBS), full deposit guarantees via SNB segregated account under Banking Act §23, 5-billion integration capital committed upfront by UBS, and explicit AT1 write-down sequence locked in binding term sheet. Coordinated public announcement set for Saturday 6 AM with deposits clearing Friday night.
minority_objections: AT1 representative repeatedly warned that leaving AT1 treatment out of the public Saturday statement (relegating it to term sheet fine print) would trigger litigation Monday despite binding language
Wealth client demanded Friday-night cleared balances visible in client portals, not Saturday morning, to prevent Friday afternoon outflows
key_conflicts: UBS demanded operational isolation of segregated account from integration costs as non-negotiable board condition; Federal Council initially unclear on scope
Tension over Saturday vs Sunday announcement timing—depositors needed Friday-night confidence lock, but UBS board signature required midnight term sheet
AT1 representative vs FINMA on whether loss waterfall must appear in public Saturday headline or only in creditor notice
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to 45-billion hard cap with no reset triggers or renegotiation—UBS absorbs tail risk beyond that ceiling
UBS accepted first-loss position on initial 5 billion of legacy losses in exchange for 45-billion government backstop above that
SNB accelerated deposit transfer to Friday 20:00 execution with real-time balance posting by 19:15 to prevent Friday afternoon run
FINMA agreed to publish AT1 waterfall in separate creditor notice rather than Saturday headline to avoid depositor confusion
red_lines: UBS: no signature without operational isolation clause ring-fencing integration capital from legacy-loss cap
UBS: deposits fully guaranteed, legacy losses capped at maximum 45 billion (with UBS taking first 5 billion), integration capital 5 billion minimum committed upfront
Federal Council: 45-billion cap must be hard ceiling with no reset or triggers to keep taxpayer exposure defensible
AT1 representative: AT1 write-down sequence must be in binding term sheet with no post-close renegotiation to prevent litigation
Wealth client: cleared deposit balances must be visible in client systems Friday night, not Saturday morning
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: No discussion of what happens if UBS walks after midnight—no fallback plan articulated beyond 'resolution protocols'
Integration cost overruns: room assumed UBS balance sheet absorbs all integration costs, but no mechanism discussed for verifying or enforcing that boundary
Cross-border contagion or international regulatory reaction to AT1 write-down not mentioned
Operational execution risk of Friday-night deposit transfer at scale—tested twice but no contingency if real-time posting fails
downstream_risk_variables: Whether wealth managers' systems actually display cleared balances with §23 reference by 19:30 Friday as promised
Whether UBS board signs at 11 PM or walks on isolation clause language
Whether Saturday 6 AM coordinated announcement (UBS acquisition + SNB mechanics + FINMA confirmation) lands simultaneously without leaks
Whether AT1 creditors accept separate creditor notice or challenge the structure Monday despite binding term sheet language
Whether 45-billion legacy-loss cap proves sufficient or whether actual losses exceed it, triggering UBS tail-risk absorption
uncertainty_notes: Term sheet signature at 11 PM Friday remains contingent on UBS board acceptance of isolation clause and AT1 sequence language. If UBS walks, no alternative buyer or resolution path was discussed. Real-time deposit posting by 19:15 Friday is operationally untested at full scale. AT1 litigation risk remains despite binding language if creditors perceive hierarchy inversion. Integration cost boundary enforcement mechanism undefined.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council R1: 'if it's just emergency lending with no resolution path, the market won't see safety, they'll see delay'—drove the room to demand binding merger terms, not just ELA
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution—drove 45B cap, 5B integration capital, isolation clause, Saturday announcement deadline, and 11 PM term sheet signature requirement
marker_evidence.government_support: Government guarantees (deposit protection, 45B legacy-loss cap, §23 statutory account) were non-negotiable conditions—UBS CEO R2: 'Deposits fully guaranteed, legacy losses capped at 8 billion—that's my floor. Below that, we walk.'
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client ultimatums drove Friday-night deposit transfer execution (19:15 real-time posting), Saturday 6 AM announcement timing, and exact statement wording—R2: 'if it's ambiguous, I'm moving my funds Monday regardless'
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down sequence became binding term sheet requirement and drove separate creditor notice—AT1 rep R2: 'if AT1 gets haircut, I'm advising creditors to challenge this in court the moment it closes. You need that locked before midnight'
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Raised repeatedly by AT1 rep (hierarchy inversion risk, litigation threat) but did not change the outcome—room proceeded with AT1 haircut in term sheet and separate creditor notice, accepting residual litigation risk
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 litigation risk acknowledged throughout (R2, R3, R4, R8, R9, R10) but treated as manageable via binding term sheet language and creditor notice—did not block the deal or alter AT1 treatment
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Midnight term sheet deadline and Saturday 6 AM announcement drove isolation clause drafting (30-min turnaround), SNB legal 10-min review, Friday 20:00 deposit transfer execution—Federal Council R2: 'I need SNB to walk me through exposure... I'm not negotiating blind'
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Mentioned as background motivation (R2 wealth client: 'market still wakes up Sunday night terrified') but did not drive specific decisions—Saturday announcement timing was driven by Friday deposit-flight risk, not Monday market panic
